$comment: Example hass-mcp configuration. Copy to 'hass-mcp.json' and edit.
Layering: built-in defaults -> this file -> environment variables.
This file is the baseline; any environment variable listed below wins over it.
Search order (first match wins):
1. $HASS_MCP_CONFIG_FILE            (explicit path; an invalid path is an error)
2. ./hass-mcp.json                  (or .hass-mcp.json, hass-mcp.yaml, hass-mcp.yml)
3. $HASS_MCP_CONFIG_DIR/hass-mcp.json
4. ~/.hass-mcp/hass-mcp.json
5. /etc/hass-mcp/hass-mcp.json
Every section and key is optional; omitted values fall back to the defaults
shown here. Keys beginning with '$' are ignored, so these notes are safe to keep.

home_assistant.$comment: Connection to Home Assistant. Env: HA_URL, HA_TOKEN, HA_SSL_VERIFY.
$comment_ssl_verify: true            - verify using the system CA store (default)
"/path/ca.pem" - verify against a custom CA bundle

$comment: MCP transport. Env: MCP_TRANSPORT, MCP_HOST, MCP_PORT (PORT is also
accepted as a fallback for Smithery). host and port apply only to the
'sse' and 'streamable-http' transports.
$comment_sessions: Session behaviour, HTTP transports only (stdio has no request layer).
Env: MCP_STATELESS_HTTP, MCP_JSON_RESPONSE, MCP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT,
MCP_MAX_SESSIONS.
streamable-http is stateful by default: the server issues an
Mcp-Session-Id on initialize and keeps that session in memory.
stateless_http        false - true disables sessions entirely. REQUIRED
to run more than one replica, since
sessions pin a client to one process
(a scale-out also needs the Redis cache
backend, not the per-process memory one)
json_response         false - true returns application/json instead of
text/event-stream; helps basic clients
and SSE-hostile proxies, loses streaming
session_idle_timeout   1800 - seconds before an idle session is ended;
its ID then 404s and the client must
initialize again
max_sessions          10000 - ceiling on concurrent sessions, a memory
bound; lower it if the port is reachable
from anywhere untrusted
Note sessions carry no credentials: bearer auth is evaluated per request,
so in allow_ha_tokens mode a client must send its Home Assistant token
on every request, not just on initialize. See docs/configuration.md.
$comment_log_level: DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR. INFO includes per-request lines naming
entity IDs and search queries, which are personal data; WARNING drops
those and keeps errors. See docs/privacy.md.

$comment: MCP bearer authentication. Required whenever server.transport is
'streamable-http' or 'sse' - the server refuses to start otherwise.
stdio is unaffected: it has no request layer and nothing is enforced.
Env: MCP_AUTH_TOKENS (comma-separated), MCP_ALLOW_HA_TOKENS.
How an incoming 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' is handled:
1. no bearer header                 -> 401
2. token listed in 'tokens'         -> accepted; Home Assistant calls
use home_assistant.token
3. token not listed, and
allow_ha_tokens is true          -> accepted; the token is used as
that request's Home Assistant
token instead of the configured
one, so each client can bring
its own credential
4. token not listed, and
allow_ha_tokens is false         -> 401
Prefer supplying these via the environment rather than committing them.
Which MCP tools are exposed to clients.
Env: MCP_TOOLS_ENABLED, MCP_TOOLS_DISABLED (both comma-separated).
'enabled' is an allow-list. Omit it or leave it empty for the default set;
use the single entry "all" to expose everything. 'disabled' is subtracted
from whatever 'enabled' produced, so you can trim the defaults without
restating them:
"tools": { "disabled": ["restart_ha"] }        - defaults minus one
"tools": { "enabled": ["all"] }                 - everything
"tools": { "enabled": ["get_entity", "list_items"] }  - just these two
The list below is the default set, written out explicitly. An unknown name
is logged as a warning and ignored rather than failing startup.
$comment_disabled: Tools available but NOT exposed by default (79 of 114).
Most are the pre-consolidation originals superseded by the unified tools
above; they still work, and adding a name to 'enabled' exposes it. Listing
them here keeps the trade-off visible: every exposed tool costs tokens in
Replaced by: list_items / get_item / manage_item / get_item_entities /
Ported from the FriendlyVoid/hass-mcp fork, and off by default for their
own reasons rather than being superseded:
call_api                 - generic REST passthrough. Forwards arbitrary
requests with the server's Home Assistant
contract, and neither reads nor invalidates
reload_automations_tool  - reload automations after editing YAML outside
Home Assistant. Not needed for automations
Ported from the nnion/hass-mcp fork (author: Nils Nilsson), read-only
diagnostics that answer narrow operational questions:
get_automation_traces_tool  - what an automation/script actually did on a
get_available_updates_tool  - components with a pending update.
get_hacs_info_tool          - HACS repositories; needs HACS installed.

$comment: Access policy: read-only mode, entity allowlist and control denylist.
Env: HASS_MCP_READ_ONLY, HASS_MCP_ENTITY_ALLOWLIST,
HASS_MCP_CONTROL_DENYLIST (comma-separated), plus
HASS_MCP_ENTITY_ALLOWLIST_FILE / HASS_MCP_CONTROL_DENYLIST_FILE.
Ported from paultanger/ha-mcp-server, but with every control OFF by
default so that upgrading changes nothing. The values below are this
project's defaults, i.e. no restrictions at all:
read_only         false - writes allowed
entity_allowlist  []    - EMPTY ALLOWS EVERYTHING (fail-open)
control_denylist  []    - empty denies nothing (fail-open)
Both lists take exact entity IDs or fnmatch globs ('sensor.gpu_*',
'lock.*'). Once entity_allowlist has any entry it becomes
authoritative and anything unmatched is denied, for reads and writes.
control_denylist is a permanent floor: a listed entity can be read but
never controlled, even when it passes the allowlist.
Policy is fixed for the process lifetime — reads are filtered inside
cached functions, so changing it means restarting the server.
$comment_fork_proposal: THE SOURCE FORK'S PROPOSED CONFIGURATION (not applied here).
paultanger/ha-mcp-server ships the opposite posture: read-only out of
the box, with a FAIL-CLOSED allowlist where an empty list denies
everything. Its rationale is that an LLM with a Home Assistant token
should start with no ability to act, and be granted capabilities
explicitly, entity by entity. Its allowlist is also independent of
Home Assistant's own Assist exposure list, which is the reason that
fork exists.
Adopting it here means setting all three, and the allowlist is then
mandatory — with read_only off and an empty allowlist you would deny
every read:
"policy": {
"read_only": true,
"entity_allowlist": [
"light.living_room",
"sensor.gpu_*",
"binary_sensor.*_offline"
"control_denylist": ["lock.*", "cover.garage_*", "alarm_control_panel.*"]
That fork also gates whole tool groups behind capability flags
(HASS_MCP_ENABLE_CONTROL, HASS_MCP_ENABLE_PROMPTS, ...). That role is
filled here by the 'tools' section above, which is per-tool rather
than per-group, so the flags were not ported. The equivalent of their
control group being off is listing the write tools in tools.disabled:
"tools": { "disabled": ["manage_item", "entity_action",
"call_service_tool", "restart_ha"] }
For long lists, keep patterns in a file instead — one per line, '#'
starts a comment:
"entity_allowlist_file": "/etc/hass-mcp/allowlist.txt"

$comment: Response caching. Env: HASS_MCP_CACHE_ENABLED, HASS_MCP_CACHE_BACKEND,
HASS_MCP_CACHE_DEFAULT_TTL, HASS_MCP_CACHE_MAX_SIZE,
HASS_MCP_CACHE_REDIS_URL, HASS_MCP_CACHE_DIR.
$comment_endpoints: Per-endpoint TTL overrides, in seconds. Four equivalent spellings, mixable:
A domain TTL applies to operations without their own entry.

$comment: Semantic entity search. Disabled by default; requires the 'vectordb' extra
(uv sync --extra vectordb). Env: HASS_MCP_VECTOR_DB_ENABLED,
HASS_MCP_VECTOR_DB_BACKEND, HASS_MCP_VECTOR_DB_PATH,
HASS_MCP_VECTOR_DB_COLLECTION, and HASS_MCP_* per key below.
vector_db.$comment_backend: One of: chroma, qdrant, weaviate, pinecone

$comment: model: sentence-transformers | openai | cohere.
Env: HASS_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL, HASS_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME,
HASS_MCP_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS, HASS_MCP_EMBEDDING_DEVICE.
